candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — understanding provider roles for coordination of maternal and primary care
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the broad nationally described CNM role across reproductive, primary, childbirth, postpartum, and newborn care while confirming that actual legal authority and practice requirements remain jurisdiction-specific.

options.A: CNM care is limited to prenatal visits and childbirth, with postpartum and primary care transferred to other clinicians.
options.B: CNMs may provide prenatal, childbirth, postpartum, gynecologic, family-planning, primary, and newborn care, subject to jurisdiction requirements.
options.C: CNMs practice only in hospitals and birth centers, so office, public-health, and home settings are outside the role.
options.D: CNMs have identical legal authority in every state because national certification creates a uniform scope of practice.

candidate.rationale: B is correct. NCSBN's current APRN Consensus Model Toolkit describes the CNM role as providing a full range of primary health care services throughout the lifespan, including gynecologic care, family planning, preconception care, prenatal and postpartum care, childbirth, and newborn care, in diverse settings. NCSBN also states that APRN regulatory requirements continue to differ by jurisdiction. A is incorrect because the nationally described CNM role extends beyond prenatal care and childbirth. C is incorrect because NCSBN explicitly includes settings such as homes, hospitals, birth centers, private offices, and community/public-health clinics. D is incorrect because national certification does not create identical legal authority across states; APRNs must meet the regulatory requirements of the jurisdiction in which the patient is located.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The nationally described CNM role spans primary and reproductive health care, pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care in diverse settings, while actual APRN regulatory authority remains jurisdiction-specific.
candidate.source_document_title: APRN Consensus Model Toolkit; APRN Consensus Model
candidate.source_locator: APRN Consensus Model Toolkit — Scope of Practice — Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM): full range of primary health care services, including gynecologic care, family planning, preconception care, prenatal and postpartum care, childbirth, and newborn care, delivered in diverse settings including home, hospital, birth center, offices, and community/public-health clinics. APRN Consensus Model — Moving Toward Uniformity: states have not adopted all Consensus Model elements, regulatory requirements differ from state to state, and APRNs must meet requirements where the patient is located.

candidate.stem: A client receiving prenatal care from a certified nurse-midwife (CNM) asks what care a CNM may provide. Which response by the RN is most accurate?
